O.outcome_detail: 21-item mathematics assessment administered after four weeks

cells.quote: In comparing the Khan Academy class and traditional math supplemental class, there was no difference in test scores , t(60) = -1.009, p = .842.
cells.note: The study used a post-test-only control-group quasi-experimental design; students were not randomly assigned.

D.treatment: more topics mastered in Khan Academy
D.comparison: fewer topics mastered in Khan Academy

cells.quote: Student assessment scores were positively correlated with both topics mastered (r(37) = .51, p = .001) and points attained (r(37) = .41, p = .009).
cells.note: This is a measured association within the Khan Academy treatment group, not a causal comparison.

D.treatment: more points attained in Khan Academy
D.comparison: fewer points attained in Khan Academy

cells.quote: Student assessment scores were positively correlated with both topics mastered (r(37) = .51, p = .001) and points attained (r(37) = .41, p = .009).
cells.note: This is a measured association within the Khan Academy treatment group, not a causal comparison.

D.comparison: combined math and ELA supplemental instruction controls

cells.quote: Analysis revealed unremarkable differences in mean post-assessment scores between the combined math and ELA supplement control (M = 72.22, SD = 14.750) and treatment (M = 73.75, SD = 14.280) groups. Although the treatment group scored slightly higher (MD = 1.53), differences did not rise to a level of statistical significance (p = .596).
cells.note: The study used a post-test only control-group quasi-experimental design; no equivalence test or adequate-power analysis was reported.
